text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Moslem-Croat federation prime minister Edhem Bicakcic said there is no "D-Day" for termination of custom privileges allowed for special categories of the population.
- Bicakcic called on local media to apologise to the federation government for causing alarm by inaccurately reporting that custom privileges would expire as of July 31.

- NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, during meeting with the members of Bosnia's collective presidency and Council of Ministers, said the NATO was determined to implement an agreement regarding the opening of airports in Tuzla, Mostar and Banja Luka.

- Bosnian ambassador to Croatia, Kasim Trnka, said Moslem and Croatian experts reached an agreement on final text of document for forthcoming meeting between chairman of presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman.
- State radio and television union considers cutting back programming or calling a strike because of difficult financial situation and unresolved legal status of company.
- Minimum level of pensions in the Moslem-Croat federation will increase from 60 to 70 German marks ($38) as of August 8, says prime minister Bicakcic.
- Forming of police authorities in all six Mostar municipalities will be completed by August 1, cantonal governor Fatima Leho said.
- Some 200 Moslem refugees returned last week to the Croat-controlled town of Jajce, Kris Janowski, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, said.

- Co-chairman of the Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, said federation towns of Tuzla and Mostar should not be punished if Serb authorities reject plan to open Banja Luka airport. If an agreement cannot be agreed with Serb autohrities, the two regional airports in the federation should be reopened for civilian flights in the meantime, he said. -- Sarajevo Newsroom, +387-71-663-864
